note: Realistic filled-in states in the scoring engine's shape. `expected` is computed by `bin/test-personas --update` and verified by `bin/test-personas`.

personas.name: routine-dysphagia-barium-swallow-complete
personas.description: Well-formed routine referral: progressive dysphagia, barium swallow requested (first-line), no pregnancy or contrast-risk factors, every completeness field including the IR(ME)R justification present — expect usually-appropriate + ok safety + low dose + routine + accept.

request.clinicalQuestion: Progressive difficulty swallowing solids over 3 months — assess for stricture or motility disorder.
request.relevantHistory: No previous GI surgery. No known allergies.

safety.irMeRJustification: Clinically indicated to investigate progressive dysphagia; no non-ionising alternative provides equivalent functional assessment.

triage.notes: Speech and language therapy also involved.

firedRules.description: Requested barium-swallow study is the recommended examination for "dysphagia".
Estimated radiation-dose band for a barium-swallow study is low.
No safety contraindications or cautions identified.
No acuity escalation; triage follows the requested urgency (routine).

personas.name: urgent-suspected-obstruction-water-soluble-aspiration-caution
personas.description: Suspected small bowel obstruction with a documented aspiration risk: a water-soluble contrast swallow is the recommended (ideal) study for the suspected-obstruction indication, and the indication itself auto-escalates triage to urgent regardless of the routine urgency requested; the aspiration risk independently forces a safety caution band (favouring water-soluble contrast over barium, which this request already correctly does) — expect usually-appropriate + caution safety + low dose + urgent + accept.

request.clinicalQuestion: Bilious vomiting and abdominal distension for 2 days — assess for small bowel obstruction and transit.
request.relevantHistory: Previous laparotomy for appendicectomy 15 years ago (adhesion risk). Reduced swallow safety noted by SALT.

safety.irMeRJustification: Urgent contrast study to confirm level and cause of suspected obstruction; water-soluble contrast chosen given aspiration risk.

triage.notes: Surgical team aware; NG tube in situ.

firedRules.description: Requested water-soluble-contrast-swallow study is the recommended examination for "suspected-obstruction".
Estimated radiation-dose band for a water-soluble-contrast-swallow study is low.
Aspiration risk — caution; favour water-soluble (non-ionic, low-osmolar) contrast over barium.

flags.suggestedAction: Favour water-soluble (low-osmolar non-ionic) contrast; avoid barium and high-osmolar agents.

personas.name: redirect-suspected-perforation-barium-contraindicated-incomplete
personas.description: Suspected oesophageal perforation (Boerhaave syndrome) after forceful vomiting, phoned through from the emergency department: barium swallow was requested, but water-soluble contrast is the recommended study for suspected-perforation and barium is contraindicated when perforation is suspected (peritonitis / mediastinitis risk) — this forces the safety band to contraindicated and, uniquely for this engine, the recommendation to redirect (not query-referrer) since barium-for-perforation has a clear safe redirect target; the indication independently forces emergency triage; several administrative fields are not yet captured — expect contraindicated safety + emergency + redirect, completeness below 100.

request.relevantHistory: Sudden severe chest and epigastric pain after forceful vomiting (suspected Boerhaave syndrome). Surgical team requesting an urgent contrast swallow.

triage.notes: Phoned through from the emergency department; cardiothoracic surgery also involved.

expected.recommendationLabel: Redirect to a more suitable study

firedRules.description: Requested barium-swallow study is not usually appropriate for "suspected-perforation"; query the referrer.
Estimated radiation-dose band for a barium-swallow study is low.
Barium study requested when perforation is suspected — contraindicated; redirect to a water-soluble contrast study.

flags.description: Barium study requested when perforation is suspected (barium peritonitis / mediastinitis risk).
flags.suggestedAction: Redirect to a water-soluble contrast study; do not use barium.
Query the referrer for the specific question the study should answer.
